title: Splash Alert! Teens Battle It Out in the Pool at the 2026 U.S. Junior Nationals
summary: The pool is buzzing, the crowd is cheering, and the fastest young swimmers in the country are giving it their all! At the 2026 U.S. Junior National Championships, every race is a nail-biter. On Day 5, the morning prelims (that's the first round of races to decide who goes to the finals) were packed with drama. In the girls' 200 IM—that's a race where swimmers do butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, and freestyle, all in one go—Gabi Brito from Beach Cities Alpha was the star. She hadn't swum any individual events all week because she was saving her energy for relays, but she jumped into the 200 IM and blew everyone away. Her butterfly split (the time for just the butterfly part) was almost a full second faster than anyone else's—28.18 seconds! She touched the wall first in 2:17.61, just a bit off her season-best. But making the final wasn't easy. The difference between 5th and 16th place was less than a second! Swimmers like Adalyn Lee, Ava Buhrman, and Nikko Tjahaya all dug deep to post times in the 2:18 range and grab spots in the 'A' final. On the boys' side, Syunta Lee is the one to watch in the 200 IM. The 16-year-old already won the 400 IM earlier in the week and set a personal best of 2:02.11 in the 200 IM just last week. That's super fast—like swimming the length of a football field in four different styles and finishing in just over two minutes! In the splash-and-dash 50 freestyle, Adalynn Biegler and Stella Canoles are the top girls. Biegler won the 100 free on Tuesday, and Canoles is the top seed with a 25.47—that's less than half a minute to zoom down the pool! For the boys, defending champion Brody Chandler is the man to beat. The 18-year-old Tennessee commit won last year in 22.52 and just reset his personal best to 22.38. He also won the 100 free earlier in the meet with a personal best of 49.77. With finals coming up, the energy is electric. Who will rise to the top? Grab your goggles and stay tuned!
why_it_matters: Seeing kids not much older than you working super hard to reach their goals can inspire you to find a sport or hobby you love and practice with heart.

Swimming races are often held in 50-meter pools, and the 200 IM is a true test of all-around skill because it mixes the four strokes without stopping.
A 50-meter freestyle race is so short and fast that swimmers might take only one breath the whole way.
